workspace.domainMeaning: UI/DTO-facing name for the `tenants` table -- the app-scoping isolation unit; related but distinct from `organizations` (legal/billing parent, 1:1 in practice via provisioning, not schema-enforced)
workspace.canonicalTenantIdentifier: tenants.id (delivered as JWT app_metadata claim named "org_id")
keyFindings: Resolved the module's central identity question with a precise, non-obvious finding: WORKSPACE_TENANT_RELATIONSHIP = SAME_ENTITY -- 'workspace' is purely the UI/DTO-facing name for the `tenants` database table (ProvisionWorkspaceDto.workspaceName/workspaceSlug write directly into tenants.name/tenants.slug, confirmed by direct read of WorkspaceProvisioningService.provision()), while `organizations` is a genuinely distinct legal/billing parent entity (CNPJ, billing_status, industry) in a tenants.org_id FK relationship, 1:1 in practice via provisioning but not schema-enforced. CANONICAL_TENANT_IDENTIFIER resolved precisely: the JWT claim used everywhere for tenant resolution is NAMED 'org_id' but its real runtime value, written by WorkspaceProvisioningService, is always `tenants.id` (`app_metadata: {org_id: membership.tenant_id, ...}`) -- a confusing naming artifact from an earlier design, not a semantic pointer to the organizations table. Confirmed self-consistent against TenantBootstrapResolver's 3-way OR match query.

Confirmed provisioning (WorkspaceProvisioningService.provision()) is genuinely atomic and idempotent -- the strongest, cleanest create-flow found in this entire audit series (0 CREATE_MAPPING_MISMATCH). Single Postgres transaction wraps organizations+tenants+org_members inserts, guarded by two advisory locks (per-user, per-slug), with an existing-active-membership short-circuit making re-invocation a genuine no-op rather than a duplicate-creation risk. The one step outside the DB transaction (Supabase Admin API app_metadata sync) is deliberately sequenced BEFORE commit, so a Supabase-side failure correctly rolls back the entire DB write via the catch block -- no split-state (workspace exists in Postgres but JWT never gets the claim) is reachable through this code path.

Confirmed TenantGuard (core authorization chokepoint for the entire system) never trusts the client-supplied X-Tenant-ID header as an authority -- the real tenant is always resolved server-side from the verified JWT's org_id claim, with the header used ONLY as a fail-closed consistency check (ForbiddenException if it doesn't match the JWT-resolved tenant). Membership is independently re-validated from the org_members table on every request (subject to a 60s distributed-cache TTL). This closes the multi-tenant identity chain that every other module in this 24-module audit series depended on and assumed correct -- now confirmed with direct evidence rather than inherited by convention.

Confirmed no workspace-switcher exists anywhere in the frontend (exhaustive grep of TenantContext.tsx/AuthContext.tsx, zero matches) -- one JWT session carries exactly one tenant claim, set once from /auth/context and never offered as a selectable list. Notably the schema itself does NOT prevent a single auth_user_id from holding active org_members rows in multiple tenants (unique constraint is per-tenant, not global) -- so multi-tenant membership is technically possible at the data layer, but nothing in the UI or /auth/context response ever surfaces a second membership or lets a user switch to it within a session. Classified as a confirmed architectural characteristic, not a gap, absent evidence the product intends session-level switching.

Confirmed the dual role model (org_members.role legacy string + role_id RBAC FK, already documented at the service level in auth.md) is disciplined and gap-free at the schema/write level specifically for workspace membership: every create/update/assignRole call performs an atomic dual-write via MembershipRoleResolverService, and last-owner protection (assertNotLastOwner) is confirmed enforced on BOTH the role-demotion and member-removal paths, not just one.

Found a third independent instance of the 'fragmented duplicate UI surface' pattern settings.md already documented twice (billing: 3 UIs; password-change: 2 UIs): /usuarios (Usuarios.tsx) can send invites but has zero UI for listing/resending/cancelling pending invitations and shows no pending-vs-accepted status distinction (since the membership row is created immediately at invite time, before acceptance) -- while Configuracoes.tsx's 'Usuarios' tab, via the same backend, has the complete surface (teamInvites/cancelInvite/resendInvite, all confirmed wired to real endpoints).

Closed the settings.md public-registration-slug pendency: PUBLIC_REGISTRATION_SLUG_WORKSPACE_OWNED=SIM -- confirmed the slug is semantically a workspace/tenant-level property (tenants.slug, real unique column, genuinely resolved server-side by the public registration backend) -- settings.md's finding that the admin UI only ever writes it to per-user localStorage stands confirmed and unchanged, with the domain-ownership question now conclusively resolved.

Found one genuine, bounded (not unbounded) SESSION_STALENESS_GAP: TenantGuard caches resolved tenant/membership for 60s via a distributed cache -- a just-deactivated membership could retain up to 60 seconds of continued access if its cache entry was populated immediately prior to deactivation. Classified as a real but self-healing window, not a permanent isolation bypass -- not counted as a TENANT_ISOLATION_GAP. Confirmed the one genuinely cross-tenant admin surface in the entire product (GET/PATCH /billing/admin/tenants, super_admin-gated) is properly backend-authorized, not merely UI-framed like AdminAudit/AdminSupport -- and confirmed no tenant-creation capability exists in any admin panel, consistent with admin.md's finding that provisioning is the sole creation path.
